_comment: Canonical App Store listing text — single source for the listing sync (Scripts/asc/listing.py). Edit HERE, never in the ASC UI. `appInfo` fields (name/subtitle/privacyPolicyUrl) are app-level, shared across platforms; `version` fields are per-platform but identical text here (the sync writes both iOS + macOS). Limits: name/subtitle 30, keywords 100 (comma-sep, no spaces), promotionalText 170, description/whatsNew 4000. Two commitments this copy must keep (ROADMAP § Toward 1.0): privacy claims say exactly what PRIVACY.md says — nothing leaves the device unless iCloud sync is enabled, and then only setup data into the user's own account; and the interval/beat display is advertised for BOWED double stops only, never as a fretted feature. `whatsNew` is deliberately absent until there has been a first release (listing.py skips it there anyway).

en-US.description:
Nitpitch is a tuner for string players — violin, guitar, bass, and more. Born violin-first, for the way string players actually tune, and every bit as at home on a guitar or bass.

A DIAL PER STRING
Choose your instrument and every string gets its own dial, lit only by pitches near its own target. Bow two adjacent strings and the tuner reads them together, showing the interval as the beats you already listen for — the pulse rate IS the tuning error, and it stills as the fifth comes true.

BUILT FOR EARS THAT NOTICE
Sub-cent accuracy across the range, which is what tuning actually needs — a cent at A4 is about a quarter of a hertz. No octave errors: string instruments put more energy into their harmonics than their fundamental, which is what makes naive tuners jump octaves, and Nitpitch's detector is built to resolve exactly that. For the last fraction of a cent, a strobe band shows sub-cent error as motion — crawling sharp or flat, stationary when true.

YOUR ORCHESTRA'S A
The reference pitch steps a hertz at a time, A=390 through 466 — 440 by default, 442 or 443 for many European orchestras, 415 for baroque ensembles. Temperaments too: equal, or pure fifths — the default on bowed instruments, because that is how string players tune.

INSTRUMENTS YOU OWN
Each instrument remembers its tuning, reference and lock exactly as you left it. Favorites sit on the launch screen with one-tap preset pins. Save your own presets, rename them, pin them — and any shape can be strung up: a 9-string guitar is a creation choice, not a missing feature.

SHARE A TUNING
Any preset becomes a QR code or a link: a bandmate scans it and gets the whole setup — strings, reference, temperament. Nothing but the setup travels, and it is never sent to any server. A collection of ready-made tunings lives at nitpitch.app.

PRIVATE BY CONSTRUCTION
Audio is analyzed in memory and discarded: no recording, no history, nothing derived from it kept. The app makes no network connections — the Mac version does not even hold the entitlement to open one. Optional iCloud sync, off until you turn it on, moves only your setups between your own devices through your own iCloud account; there is no server of ours, and no ability to read what syncs.

FOR THE WHOLE SECTION
Violin, viola, cello, double bass, guitar, bass guitar — and a chromatic mode for everything else. Native on iPhone, iPad, and Mac; on the Mac, plugging an electric instrument into an audio interface gives the detector a cleaner signal than any microphone in a room.

Free and open source (MIT). No ads, no accounts, no tracking.
en-US.promotionalText: A tuner for violin, guitar, bass, and more: a dial per string, bowed double stops read as the beats you hear, sub-cent precision. No ads, no accounts, no tracking.
